candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record supports sarcoidosis as the unifying diagnosis: noncaseating granulomatous hepatitis on liver biopsy, multiorgan involvement (liver, spleen, skull bones), polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia, PTH-independent hypercalcemia (low PTH 9 ng/L consistent with 1,25-OH2D3-mediated mechanism), negative tuberculin test, and no evidence of malignancy or other granulomatous disease. The candidate label 'Sarcoidosis with hypercalcemia' is a complete equivalent of the reference 'sarcoidosis'; the added qualifier is a documented manifestation integral to the case rather than a conflicting or narrowing subtype.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Sarcoidosis with hypercalcemia is the same diagnostic entity as sarcoidosis; the hypercalcemia is a well-known manifestation of sarcoidosis and its explicit inclusion does not conflict with or narrow the reference diagnosis—it merely names a prominent feature already present in the case.

case_quality_flags: Hypercalcemia recurrence despite zoledronate is consistent with ongoing granuloma-mediated calcitriol production, further supporting sarcoidosis over malignancy.
Bone marrow biopsy and labial salivary gland biopsy were unremarkable, but liver biopsy was diagnostic—case well-supported for sarcoidosis.
